body:
**Stable key:** `MEM-AUTO`  
**Difficulty:** **High**  
**Suggested label:** `difficulty:high` (metadata proposal; a title/body marker does not depend on label availability)  
**Planning baseline:** `Ozwasyd/FsusBlog@580cf1af614fd0edab9cb4c9ee95ec4e128b0327`  
**Acceptance predecessors:** `MEM-P02` (#3446), `MEM-P03` (#3447), `MEM-P04` (#3448), `MEM-P08` (#3450), `MEM-P09` (#3452)

### Objective

Implement the user's default behavior: detect automatically, activate and select automatically when support, qualification, and admission permit it, allow explicit manual shutdown, and recover automatically without hidden opt-ins.

### Source and scope precedence

This issue implements the clarified default-automation requirement in addition to the report. The user's later requirement for default automatic discovery and activation supersedes `Preferred`, default-off, and mandatory manual-per-capability opt-in wording. Original work-item IDs are preserved for traceability. Baseline paths must be checked against the actual implementation candidate; this issue is not a claim that proposed types already exist.

### Mandatory policy and terminology

All configurable capabilities default to `Auto` when omitted. `Auto` means automatic discovery, bounded qualification, online activation, and deterministic selection for an eligible workload after resource admission. It does not mean indiscriminate allocation. A supported, release-qualified and runtime-qualified available path must not require a second enable flag, per-host approval file, or administrator confirmation. `Disabled` prevents new capability-specific probes and use, and drains existing owners before disposal. `Required` adds a strict requirement; it does not override safety, permissions, qualification, or budgets. The earlier report value `Preferred` is superseded, not an additional mode.

Detection, qualification, online state, effective path, and per-operation admission are separate facts. Unknown, Unsupported, NotVerified, Faulted, Disabled, and temporarily BudgetRejected are not synonyms. A missing signal is not zero usage. Qualifying a release/backend is not a manual opt-in on each deployment. The always-required accounting, ownership, and content-security rules are not optional capability switches.

### Scope and exclusions

No automatic installation of drivers or packages, BIOS/OS-global policy changes, unbounded startup benchmarking, unsafe capability forcing, or new HTTP behavior is included.

All product implementation introduced by this memory program remains C#/.NET. Supported already-installed OS/GPU APIs may be called through isolated C# adapters. Existing unrelated C++, frontend, protocol, and business components are not rewritten. Do not change AEDS/HTTP, authorization, revocation, publication, or delivery authority merely to simplify memory management.

### Files and ownership

| Status | Path or owner | Required treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| N | `src/backend/Infrastructure/Memory/Capabilities/` | The single capability registry, policy resolver, probe executor, lifecycle, and recovery controller. |
| N | `src/backend/Infrastructure/Memory/Contracts/` | Consume MEM-P02 models without redefining mode semantics. |
| N | `src/backend/Infrastructure/Memory/Accounting/` | Reserve probe and recovery capacity through the existing coordinator. |
| N | `src/backend/Infrastructure/Memory/Pressure/` | Consume source quality and identity; do not turn Unknown into eligibility. |
| R | `Existing runtime configuration, startup, readiness, and protected diagnostics owners` | Integrate activation and reporting at existing boundaries. |
| N | `Automatic-capability tests inside the canonical backend test project` | A01-A20; register them in tests/matrix.yml. |

B = baseline-reported; N = proposed-new; R = exact owner unresolved until MEM-P00. Paths and namespaces in this table are scope locators, not permission to create a parallel registry, publisher, scheduler, configuration source, or test runner. New tests must reside inside the actual owning project.

### Required implementation work

- [ ] **AUTO.1** Implement one registry and lifecycle controller for eligible host backends, pressure sources, disk tiers, index strategies, page/NUMA/lock/I/O capabilities, device backends, and mapped-device/P2P paths. Reuse current configuration and observability owners rather than adding a separate operational authority.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-AUTO-AC01`, `MEM-AUTO-AC15`.
- [ ] **AUTO.2** Normalize omitted settings to Auto and resolve dependencies, exclusivity, release qualification, and explicit Disabled/Required policy before capability-specific side effects. Ship applicability and qualification rules with the release; never require a per-host enable file or manual capability approval.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-AUTO-AC01`, `MEM-AUTO-AC05`, `MEM-AUTO-AC11`.
- [ ] **AUTO.3** Run bounded discovery and correctness probes through reservations and an isolated control-plane executor. Bind probe results to backend version, runtime/OS/architecture, device/driver identity, relevant permission state, and configuration revision. Cache results only while their identity and validity remain applicable.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-AUTO-AC02`, `MEM-AUTO-AC09`, `MEM-AUTO-AC13`.
- [ ] **AUTO.4** Automatically place qualified capabilities online and select effective paths deterministically for declared eligible workload classes. Keep backend online state separate from request-level admission and actual byte placement. Resource availability permits use; it does not mandate filling every available tier.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-AUTO-AC02`, `MEM-AUTO-AC07`, `MEM-AUTO-AC11`.
- [ ] **AUTO.5** Implement startup Disabled without driver loading, device context creation, mapping, staging allocation, capability-specific test writes, or retry activity. At runtime, accepted disable first denies new probes, operations, and acquisitions, then drains existing owners before disposal.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-AUTO-AC03`, `MEM-AUTO-AC04`, `MEM-AUTO-AC10`.
- [ ] **AUTO.6** Implement Required startup failure and atomic rejection of invalid runtime revisions. After a required capability is lost, fail its readiness requirement while preserving safety and performing only bounded permitted recovery. Temporary per-operation budget rejection remains a resource result, not forced overcommit.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-AUTO-AC05`, `MEM-AUTO-AC06`.
- [ ] **AUTO.7** Implement fault isolation, identity-sensitive invalidation, retry classification, backoff, and circuit breaking. Auto capabilities recover without operator re-enablement after fresh qualification and admission, but repeated faults remain bounded and visible.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-AUTO-AC06`, `MEM-AUTO-AC08`, `MEM-AUTO-AC09`, `MEM-AUTO-AC10`.
- [ ] **AUTO.8** Implement per-device and shared-domain admission for multiple devices and shared UMA. Discover all eligible devices within the configured discovery bound; select independently qualified devices without duplicate spending or accidental assumption that each device exposes independent host capacity.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-AUTO-AC07`, `MEM-AUTO-AC12`.
- [ ] **AUTO.9** Expose requested mode, detected state, qualification state, online lifecycle, effective path, per-operation admission, revision/epoch, retry state, and stable reason codes through protected existing diagnostics. Do not expose raw addresses, credentials, untrusted paths, or unbounded identifiers.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-AUTO-AC06`, `MEM-AUTO-AC09`, `MEM-AUTO-AC14`.
- [ ] **AUTO.10** Add the A01-A20 deterministic capability matrix and integrate actual backend tests as they arrive. Prove default behavior with omitted configuration, manual disable before and during use, safe recovery, dependency conflicts, stale qualification, and no hot-path probing.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-AUTO-AC01`, `MEM-AUTO-AC02`, `MEM-AUTO-AC03`, `MEM-AUTO-AC04`, `MEM-AUTO-AC05`, `MEM-AUTO-AC06`, `MEM-AUTO-AC07`, `MEM-AUTO-AC08`, `MEM-AUTO-AC09`, `MEM-AUTO-AC10`, `MEM-AUTO-AC11`, `MEM-AUTO-AC12`, `MEM-AUTO-AC13`, `MEM-AUTO-AC14`, `MEM-AUTO-AC15`, `MEM-AUTO-AC16`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC01** A01: With all capability keys absent, the normalized policy is Auto for every registered configurable capability. Explicit Auto produces the same result. No second feature flag, mandatory environment variable, or per-host approval file can prevent otherwise eligible activation.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC02** A02/A03: On an applicable release-qualified backend whose bounded self-test passes, the controller reaches Online within the configured probe/activation bounds and selects the declared path for an eligible admitted operation. No eligible workload means zero mandatory cache population, not disabled capability.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC03** A04: Startup Disabled results in zero capability-specific initialization, context creation, mapping, resource allocation, test writes, and retry probes. Cached non-invasive status may be displayed; dependency discovery must not reactivate the disabled capability.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC04** A05: Runtime Disabled is linearized before new operation admission. New work uses an admissible fallback or the original failure contract; old readers/I/O/DMA retain their resources until actual completion. The state is Draining until safe disposal, not immediately Off.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC05** A06/A07: Required with unsupported or unqualified startup dependencies prevents readiness. An invalid runtime policy revision is rejected atomically and leaves the prior accepted revision intact. Required cannot bypass budgets, permissions, qualification, or revocation.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC06** A08: Loss of an active required capability changes readiness according to the required contract and safely isolates its epoch. Auto loss chooses an admissible qualified fallback. Neither case frees uncertain DMA memory or performs a full-device/whole-disk copy into host RAM.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC07** A09/A10: Missing permissions, missing drivers, unsupported mappings, single-node NUMA, stale samples, and unqualified driver/API combinations have different reason codes. Unknown or NotVerified cannot become Qualified because hardware was merely enumerated.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC08** A11: A qualified capability with insufficient current staging/slot/space budget remains online but rejects that operation with a budget reason. Later budget recovery automatically admits eligible work without another user enable action.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC09** A12: Repeated probe or initialization failure respects finite attempt, concurrency, time, and resource bounds and the configured cooldown. A successful requalification after an allowed retry or identity change automatically restores eligible selection.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC10** A13: Manual Disabled cancels scheduling of future automatic retries and prevents completed stale probes from publishing Online. Re-enabling Auto starts a fresh permitted qualification cycle without accepting old-epoch resources.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC11** A14/A15: An identity or policy change invalidates affected qualification before new use. Required-child/Disabled-parent conflicts reject deterministically; competing backends use one recorded selection rule and do not all allocate optimistically.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC12** A16: Page locking only applies to its declared bounded eligible subset; UMA does not add independent host escape capacity; large BAR reporting alone does not authorize CPU mapping. Automatic activation does not alter those backend contracts.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC13** A17/A18: Probes use the common reservation coordinator and release their task-owned resources, including every failure path. They never change BIOS, global VM policy, swap settings, cgroup limits, device drivers, or download dependencies.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC14** A19: Instrumented L0 hits execute zero capability probes, driver loads, pressure-file reads, or backend initializations. All such work is confined to bounded control-plane transitions.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC15** A20: Omitted-config integration tests cover success, absent capability, explicit disable, pressure suspension, recovery, and runtime disable with active operations. Protected diagnostics distinguish all states and remain within the configured retention/cardinality limits.
- [ ] **MEM-AUTO-AC16** Every required A01-A20 assertion is independently observed rather than accepted from the controller's self-reported success flag. Simulators establish state-machine behavior; actual hardware qualification still requires the applicable backend evidence.

### Required validation scope

Executable lifecycle tests with bounded contract-conforming fixture backends and available real baseline backends. Hardware qualification is supplied later by MEM-P16/P17/P18 and closed by MEM-P19.

| Scenario | Responsibility in this issue | Required observable assertion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `A01`: Omitted configuration | Primary implementation owner | Every registered capability normalizes to Auto without hidden activation flags. |
| `A02`: Supported and qualified capability | Primary implementation owner | Bounded checks plus admission automatically produce Online/effective eligible use. |
| `A03`: Online capability with no eligible work | Primary implementation owner | Do not allocate merely to fill capacity; distinguish online from workload placement. |
| `A04`: Disabled at startup | Primary implementation owner | Zero capability-specific side effects, initialization, test writes, and recovery probes. |
| `A05`: Disabled during active use | Primary implementation owner | Stop new work before draining old readers/I/O/DMA; never free early. |
| `A06`: Required unavailable at startup | Primary implementation owner | Fail the declared startup/readiness requirement without unsafe fallback. |
| `A07`: Invalid runtime policy update | Primary implementation owner | Reject the revision atomically and keep the prior accepted policy/resources intact. |
| `A08`: Loss of a required or Auto capability | Primary implementation owner | Apply exact readiness/fallback behavior and safe epoch isolation. |
| `A09`: Absent capability and permission/API failures | Primary implementation owner | Emit distinct bounded reasons, not fabricated support. |
| `A10`: Unknown, stale, or unqualified identity | Primary implementation owner | Never promote detection-only or mock-only results to runtime qualification. |
| `A11`: Temporary staging/slot/space rejection | Primary implementation owner | Remain online as appropriate; reject this operation and automatically recover admission. |
| `A12`: Repeated failures and later recovery | Primary implementation owner | Bound attempts/resources/backoff and restore Auto use after permitted fresh qualification. |
| `A13`: Disable races with probe completion or recovery | Primary implementation owner | Stale completions cannot reactivate a disabled policy; retries remain stopped. |
| `A14`: Driver/device/configuration identity change | Primary implementation owner | Invalidate affected qualification and reject old-epoch results before reuse. |
| `A15`: Dependency conflicts and exclusive backends | Primary implementation owner | Reject Required-child/Disabled-parent conflicts and select one deterministic effective path. |
| `A16`: Special capability eligibility | Primary implementation owner | Lock only eligible bounded ranges; keep UMA shared; large BAR alone grants no CPU mapping. |
| `A17`: Probe resource accounting and cleanup | Primary implementation owner | Reserve first, bound every probe, and release only owned resources on all terminal paths. |
| `A18`: Scope of automatic actions | Primary implementation owner | Do not modify global OS/BIOS/driver settings, raise privileges, or download dependencies. |
| `A19`: Hot request path | Primary implementation owner | Perform no probing, driver loading, backend initialization, or pressure-file I/O on L0 hits. |
| `A20`: Full default-policy lifecycle observability | Primary implementation owner | Cover automatic activation, disable, pressure, fault, and recovery with independent bounded evidence. |

### Evidence and acceptance rules

Every unchecked acceptance criterion below is mandatory. `must` and `must not` are normative; `may` grants an option only where it is explicitly stated. A required test passes only when its specified assertion is observed on the current candidate. A comment stating that an assertion is true is not evidence.

Bind evidence to the actual commit and worktree fingerprint, fixture, toolchain, configuration revision, backend, OS/architecture, relevant driver/device identity, actual command, and raw result. Use the existing test DAG, required static admission, fixture ownership, and independent verifiers. All numeric limits and performance expressions referenced by this issue must be finite, explicit, and frozen by their owning policy/baseline before candidate results are examined. Missing values block acceptance; do not invent a passing threshold afterward.

Expected resource rejection must not conceal use-after-free, bounds violations, double free, uninitialized disclosure, revoked/wrong content, negative accounting, a parallel authority, or an unbounded queue. Any such correctness failure blocks acceptance regardless of performance. Do not rewrite frozen receipts or weaken tests. Missing platform or hardware evidence is `NotVerified`, not `Passed` or a convenient `NotApplicable`.

Evidence level is stage-specific: contract or fixture work may run before a downstream backend exists, but it does not certify that backend. Each primary implementation owner must supply its own required integration/platform evidence; MEM-P19 independently closes the complete matrix. Passing tests never authorizes automatic closure of this issue, another issue, or a pull request.

### Safe disable and rollback

Stop new transitions and operations for the affected enhancement, safely drain existing owners, and use a qualified admissible baseline. Preserve explicit Disabled and Required intent and never erase live charges.

### Completion report

Report the exact scope and files changed, every acceptance-criterion result, tests and commands actually run, raw current-source evidence, default Auto behavior, negative/competition cases, performance against frozen gates where applicable, unresolved support rows, and rollback results. A missing required environment leaves the corresponding promise unverified. Do not describe planned tests or a passing document validator as product verification.

Docker-related tests are not to be executed by this delivery agent under the project restriction. State them explicitly as not run. A Docker-specific assertion requires evidence from its authorized owner; a genuinely technology-independent assertion may use authorized non-Docker isolation. Do not fetch missing implementation dependencies from the network; record exact package/version/target gaps and stop the blocked execution item.

### Additional notes

This is a new work package introduced by the clarified requirement. It supersedes Preferred and manual-per-capability opt-in language in the original report. It does not replace backend-specific qualification, content authorities, or the memory governor.
